description: A DNE is kept in the series score even when it is the boat's worst; her next worst score is excluded instead, and discarding the DNE would change the standings.
citation: RRS 2025-2028 90.3(b): 'When a scoring system provides for excluding one or more race scores, any score that is a Disqualification Not Excludable (DNE) shall be included in a boat's series score.' A2.1 is subject to rule 90.3(b). A10: 'DNE Disqualification that is not excludable'. A5.2 scores it one more than the boats entered, and A6.1 moves the boats behind her up.
working: 5 boats entered, so DNE scores 6. One score is excluded per boat.
R2 crossing order A B C E D; A is DNE, so her place is vacated: B 1, C 2, E 3, D 4; A DNE 6.
A 1,6,2: gross 9. The DNE 6 is her worst but may not be excluded (90.3(b)), so her next worst, 2 (R3), is excluded: net 7.
B 2,1,1: gross 4, 2 (R1) excluded, net 2. C 3,2,4: gross 9, 4 (R3) excluded, net 5. E 5,3,3: gross 11, 5 (R1) excluded, net 6. D 4,4,5: gross 13, 5 (R3) excluded, net 8.
Standings: B 2, C 5, E 6, A 7, D 8.

Counterfactual: had A's DNE been excluded, she would net 1+2 = 3 and rank second, ahead of C, E and D. So a scorer that discards a DNE fails this vector on A's net and rank, not only on the excluded flag.
